gates.description: Sprint goal must be defined as a single sentence describing the sprint outcome
Impediments must be tracked with resolution authority and age
Every retrospective must produce 1-3 actionable improvements with owners and deadlines
Team velocity must be tracked as a 4-sprint rolling average for planning
Team capacity must be calculated accounting for PTO, holidays, and meetings
WIP limits must be monitored — items in progress should not exceed team size

anti_patterns.description: Using the Scrum Master role to assign work, track individual productivity, and report to management
Running ceremonies mechanically without adapting — same retro format every sprint while the team disengages
Over-protecting the team from organizational reality — creating an information vacuum
Treating velocity as the primary measure of team success — leads to point inflation and corner-cutting
Present in ceremonies but absent between them — impediments do not wait for standup
Enforcing rigid process rules when the team needs flexibility — Scrum is a framework, not a religion

escalation_triggers: A blocker has been unresolved for more than 48 hours and is impacting sprint delivery
A team member's behavior consistently undermines collaboration and coaching has not changed it
Management is pressuring the team to commit to more than velocity supports and pushback has been overridden
PM changes sprint scope repeatedly without acknowledging the cost and direct conversation has not resolved it
Team health indicators show a sustained decline over 3+ sprints
A team member raises a concern about harassment, discrimination, or hostile work environment

input_requirements.description: Groomed backlog with estimated stories and acceptance criteria

output_certifications: Sprint goal defined as a single sentence
Impediments tracked with resolution authority and age
Retrospective produces 1-3 actionable improvements with owners and deadlines
Team velocity tracked as a 4-sprint rolling average
Team capacity calculated (PTO, holidays, meetings accounted for)
